title: Comparative study of the encrustation tendency of silicone balloon catheters with anti-adhesive coating and uncoated balloon catheters
summary: The aim of the study is to demonstrate a reduction in the amount of encrustation and the infection problem with coated catheters under comparable conditions compared to uncoated catheters.

interventions.name: Coated catheters (Suprapubic and transurethral indwelling catheters, as well as transurethral catheters after radical prostatectomy)
Conventional catheters (comparator, Suprapubic and transurethral indwelling catheters, as well as transurethral catheters after radical prostatectomy)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients requiring the use of a transurethral or suprapubic indwelling catheter
- Patients after radical prostatectomy
- Expected catheter indwelling time of at least one week after medical indication
- Written informed consent is available
Exclusion criteria:
• Patients in whom a balloon catheter cannot be inserted due to anatomical conditions, particularly the transurethral CH 16 and suprapubic CH 12, 16, and 20 types
• Patients with prostatitis, urethral stricture, urethritis, or an insufficiently filled and contracted bladder
• Catheterized patients with an existing symptomatic urinary tract infection
• Insufficient mental, verbal, or physical ability to participate in the study
• ECOG >3 (Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group)
• Taking immunosuppressants
• Refusal to participate in the clinical trial
• Participation in another clinical trial within the last 30 days
• Patients who are pregnant or breastfeeding
